data.what: The no-second-figure gate assembles its search needle from characters instead of spelling the removed name.
data.why: Plan Verification V2 greps -rni for that name over apps/next/__tests__ as well as the two source roots, so a gate that spelled what it forbids would be the one line in the repo that could never pass it. Bytes compared are identical; only the test file's own text differs.
data.costIfWrong: A future reader greps for the name to find the gate and does not find it - mitigated by a docblock that says so.

data.what: Restated M6's Actors.tsx needle to the IMPERATIVE group gate and de-duplicated PRESENCE_EPS there, rather than dropping Actors.tsx from the gate.
data.why: The line the old regex matched was the removed figure's declarative visible={presence > PRESENCE_EPS}. The surviving robot gates its whole group too, but on the group ref inside the Director callback because presence is sampled per frame. Same claim, different form. Found in passing: the robot's gate used the bare literal 0.005 while PRESENCE_EPS sat imported and unused.
data.costIfWrong: None behavioural - PRESENCE_EPS is 0.005, so the swap is an identity.

data.what: Closed V17's 6% one-shot floor by holding the ending's lens at fov 40 across all three keys, not by moving the crane in.
data.why: A2 pins the crane at 2.28 -> 3.2 m, and the keys were opening 40 -> 41 -> 42 as the eye pulled back, so lens and distance compounded: 5.54% of the last frame. One lens (which A2 requires anyway) gives 6.16% with nothing moved.
data.costIfWrong: A slightly tighter closing frame than shipped; the crane's authored travel is untouched.

data.what: Gave STAGED.phone a drawn row (0.3164 x 0.67 x 0.129) rather than re-framing control-answer
data.why: Without a drawn row pieceBox gives a piece its own HEIGHT as depth, so the phone was framed as a 1.089 m deep slab where Phone.tsx's bodyBox() draws 0.210. The fit gate reads pieceBox, so every camera off the device's normal was charged for half a metre of phone that is not there. This is a box correction, not a gate relaxation: the blocking gate's containment assertion red-proves it and independently demands exactly [0.495, 0.705] on that axis.
data.costIfWrong: If the phone really were deeper than 0.129 m the fit gate would now undercharge it; the containment gate fails on any understatement, which is what was red-proved.

data.what: Left control-answer on FIT_DEBT and GRAMMAR_DEBT; did not re-frame it
data.why: With the phone box corrected the scene is 63 percent outside the fit bar at p=0.7960, not 1 percent at p=0.7857 as the previous handoff measured - the gate reports only its FIRST finding. The violation is the foreground phone bleeding off frame-left, which P4 accepted deliberately after measuring six alternative positions. Clearing it needs either a pulled-back frame (P4 says that breaks the film's one promise about refusals) or a declared exemption for a foreground object. Both are art-direction calls for the owner.
data.costIfWrong: If the owner wants the phone held whole, the frame must move back and the requests stamp stops reading - the two are the same lever.
